context: The target amount is 131, and the reusable denominations are [1, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100]. At each step, choose the largest denomination that does not exceed the remaining amount.
description: In each of the first four steps, the highlighted coin is the next one to use. Deduct it on the way to the following step. Gray means the coin is unselected in this step and can still be used later. At step five, the amount reaches zero, the row of coins disappears, and selection stops.
prose.result: This example uses 4 coins, the minimum possible. For other sets of denominations, greedy selection need not be optimal.

steps.announcement: Start with 131 and select the largest usable denomination, 100. Deducting it will leave 31.
steps.explanation: Start with 131 and 0 coins used. Of the available denominations, 100 comes closest to 131 without exceeding it. Select 100 now. It has yet to be deducted, so the next state will have 131 - 100 = 31 left.
steps.key_state: Remaining amount: 131. Coins already used: none (0 coins). Next coin selected: 100, still to be deducted.
steps.title: Remaining amount 131: choose 100, the largest usable coin

steps.announcement: After deducting 100, the remaining amount is 31. Choose 20 next. Deducting it will leave 11.
steps.explanation: Deducting the previous coin, 100, leaves 31. One coin, 100, has been used. Denominations 50 and 100 both exceed 31, and the largest denomination that fits is 20. The highlighted 20 is the next coin. It has yet to be deducted and will leave 31 - 20 = 11.
steps.key_state: Remaining amount: 31. One coin already used (100). Next coin selected: 20, still to be deducted.
steps.title: Remaining amount 31: 100 has been deducted, and 20 is next

steps.announcement: After deducting 20, the remaining amount is 11. Choose 10 next. Deducting it will leave 1.
steps.explanation: Deducting the previous coin, 20, leaves 11. The 2 coins used so far, 100 and 20, total 120. Denominations 20, 50, and 100 all exceed 11, and the largest denomination that fits is 10. Select 10 as the next coin. It has yet to be deducted and will leave 11 - 10 = 1.
steps.key_state: Remaining amount: 11. Two coins already used (100, 20). Next coin selected: 10, still to be deducted.
steps.title: Remaining amount 11: two coins used, and 10 is next

steps.announcement: After deducting 10, the remaining amount is 1. Choose 1 next. Deducting it will leave zero.
steps.explanation: Deducting the previous coin, 10, leaves 1. The 3 coins used so far, 100, 20, and 10, total 130. Denominations 5, 10, 20, 50, and 100 all exceed 1. Only the smallest denomination, 1, fits. Select it now. It has yet to be deducted and will leave 1 - 1 = 0.
steps.key_state: Remaining amount: 1. Three coins already used (100, 20, 10). Next coin selected: 1, still to be deducted.
steps.title: Remaining amount 1: three coins used, and the last coin is 1

steps.announcement: Deducting 1 brings the amount to zero. A total of 4 coins make change for 131.
steps.explanation: Deducting the fourth coin, 1, leaves 0. The row of candidate coins disappears, and selection stops. The four rounds used 4 coins, 100, 20, 10, and 1, with a total value of 100 + 20 + 10 + 1 = 131. Denominations 5 and 50 were unused.
steps.key_state: Remaining amount: 0. The 4 coins used (100, 20, 10, 1) make 131, completing the change.
steps.title: Remaining amount zero: four coins complete the change

prose.summary: The five steps show the remaining amount before each of four coin choices and the final state after the last deduction.
prose.title: Coin change: making 131

context: The target amount is 131, and the available denominations are [1, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100]. Each denomination can be used repeatedly. The figure states the greedy rule: “Always choose the coin closest to the remaining amount without exceeding it.” In each round, this is the largest denomination that fits.
description: From top to bottom, the rows show remaining amounts of 131, 31, 11, 1, and 0. The first four rows show the same denominations in the same order. They highlight 100, 20, 10, and 1 in turn, with the other denominations in gray. Dashed arrows link the choices in consecutive rows. The last row reaches zero and shows no candidate coins.

The remaining amount in each row already accounts for the coins used earlier. The highlighted coin is the next one, and its value is still included in the current amount. For example, the row for 31 has already deducted 100. Its highlighted 20 is deducted on the way to the row for 11. For each remaining amount, the table lists the coins already used, the next coin, and the amount left after that deduction.

frames.explanation: The final 4 coins give 100 + 20 + 10 + 1 = 131. Denominations 5 and 50 are unused. For these denominations, 4 is also the minimum coin count. With other denominations, the greedy rule may use more coins than necessary.
frames.title: Four greedy choices reduce the remaining amount from 131 to zero

summary: At each round, choose the largest denomination that does not exceed the remaining amount. The figure follows this process from 131 down to zero.

tables.caption: Remaining amount, coins already used, and next choice

title: Coin change: making one greedy choice at a time
